seed_ledger.name: Waha to Mexico (Wahalajara System Expansion)
seed_ledger.reason: Two turbo-compression units at San Juan in Chihuahua and Aguascalientes in Mexico, taking the system from about 1.3 to about 2 Bcf/d. Trade press says no new US pipe. Data centers appear once, as a general Mexican demand sector, not a project customer. No US data center tie, no US facility, length 0 in the US. Web search budget ran out after about 9 searches across the three seeds, so the full eight-search checklist was not met; FERC eLibrary, Railroad Commission, county records and earnings calls were not searched for this seed. Searches run: 3. Sources: Pipeline and Gas Journal March 2026 (Mexico-only work, one data center mention); Siemens Energy and Esentia releases via search (same); EIA row (power and industrial demand only).

evidence.note: expansion is Mexican compression only; data centers named as a general demand sector

seed_ledger.name: WT-0 Compressor Station Project
seed_ledger.reason: Transwestern new 13,220 hp compressor in Chaves County NM, 80,000 MMBtu/d firm service from West Texas Lateral to Panhandle Lateral, FERC CP25-37-000, 15-year open season in 2024. No source names a data center shipper. A Zenith Volts data center campus (about 1.3 GW, onsite gas generators, off grid) was approved in Chaves County in August 2025 but no source says how it gets gas or links it to WT-0. Length 0. Web search budget ran out after about 9 searches across the three seeds, so the full eight-search checklist was not met; FERC eLibrary, Railroad Commission, county records and earnings calls were not searched for this seed. Searches run: 3. Sources: FERC notice summary (compressor only, no data center); Transwestern open season notice (shipper not named); Albuquerque Journal on Zenith (gas generators, no supply route).

evidence.note: Zenith campus uses onsite gas generators; no pipeline named
